clue.text: Little Richard didn't intend covering "Kiss" — only Number Ones

indicators.note: number ones are the items at the front of each line-up, so only the leading letter of each word counts

parts.note: the opening letters of the four words in order

explanation.surface: A tale about the rock'n'roll star Little Richard refusing to cover a Kiss song, recording only chart-toppers.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Richard reads as the singer, but it is a pet form of the first name; Kiss looks like the band but is just a word supplying a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Dick is a familiar diminutive of Richard, so a small or pet form of that given name.

clue.text: Lexicographer, sure to get excited by word for new teeth

indicators.note: excited things are stirred up and agitated, so the letters get jumbled

parts.note: Susie Dent, the lexicographer in Dictionary Corner on the TV word game Countdown
the four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A dictionary expert gets excited about a new word for false teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: Susie Dent is the resident lexicographer on Countdown, the British TV letters-and-numbers quiz that runs through this puzzle as a theme.
explanation.definitionFit: False teeth fitted to replace lost natural ones are a replacement set, hence a fresh set of choppers.

clue.text: Incentive for panel game host to do send-up

parts.note: Jimmy Carr, comedian who hosts the TV panel show 8 Out of 10 Cats (Does Countdown)

indicators.note: in a down entry, sending something up makes it read from bottom to top

parts.note: 'to' taken as written, 'do' being part of the instruction

explanation.surface: A TV quiz host is offered a reward for performing a comic parody.
explanation.walkthrough: Jimmy Carr hosts 8 Out of 10 Cats Does Countdown, which ties him to the puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A reward dangled to motivate someone is the classic image of the vegetable held before a donkey.

clue.text: Scruffy type, reportedly vacant, a ponytail, short

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the sound counts rather than the spelling

parts.note: ilk means sort or kind; spoken, it matches the first part

indicators.note: being short of something means lacking it, so a piece is removed

parts.note: vacant means unoccupied
the tail, or last letter, of pony

explanation.surface: Describing a scruffy person, apparently empty-headed, whose ponytail is cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Type' is heard, not read; then 'vacant' loses its final letter, the one at the end of 'pony'.
explanation.definitionFit: Kempt is an old word for combed or tidy, so its negative describes an untidy, unkempt appearance.

clue.text: Went to a restaurant for tea (that's a clue)

definitions.meaning: first meaning: dined away from home
second meaning: read as a cryptic clue, the phrase would lead to the drink, since three letters jumbled by 'out' give it

explanation.surface: Someone went out to a restaurant for their evening meal.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer is itself a tiny cryptic clue, with 'out' as an anagram signal on the three letters before it, solving to TEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Dining in a restaurant rather than at home is the everyday phrasal-verb meaning of eating away.

clue.text: Musical jazz singing star initially held back

indicators.note: something held back is kept to the end, so a letter moves from the front to the rear

parts.note: scat is improvised wordless jazz vocalising
the letter that begins 'star' is the one moved

explanation.surface: A jazz singer, the star of a musical, is kept back at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of the jazz word is the one that 'star' begins with, and it is shunted to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andrew Lloyd Webber stage show based on T. S. Eliot's feline poems is a famous musical.

clue.text: Channel in Spooner's broad river

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so the initial sounds of two words trade places

parts.note: the Tay is Scotland's longest river; it takes the opening W sound of the other word
broad means wide; it takes the opening T sound of the river

explanation.surface: A channel described in the words of Spooner as a broad river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tay is Scotland's longest river; swapping the W and T sounds of the two words gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tideway is a channel in which a tidal current runs, or the tidal stretch of a river.

clue.text: Fish head almost blended, some pieces left on the surface

definitions.text: some pieces left on the surface

indicators.note: blended ingredients are mixed together, so these letters are mixed into a new order
the head of something is its top or front, so only the leading letter is kept

parts.note: first letter
the six letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A fish head nearly liquidised, with bits left floating on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' reads as qualifying 'blended', but it is the word that gets blended.
explanation.definitionFit: Floating wreckage or debris from a ship is bits and pieces left drifting on the water.

clue.text: Effect visible in batik, a tie-dyeing process

indicators.note: something visible within can be seen inside, so the letters lie inside the words that follow

parts.note: runs across the end of the first word, the article and the start of the third

explanation.surface: An effect you can see in batik fabric, a dyeing technique using ties.
explanation.walkthrough: Batik is itself a fabric-dyeing method, so the surface keeps the reader thinking about textiles rather than letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ikat is an Indonesian textile technique in which yarns are bound and dyed before weaving.

clue.text: Folk songs used regularly in remixed stereo links

indicators.note: a remix reworks a recording into a new version, so the letters are rearranged
regularly means at even intervals, so letters are taken at a steady spacing

parts.note: every third letter, starting with the first
taken as written

explanation.surface: Folk songs are used from time to time in stereo remixes.
explanation.walkthrough: The regular spacing here is every third letter, not the usual every other letter; those three join the six before the whole lot is mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: A reef knot is a square knot joining two rope ends, so these are ties that link lines together.

clue.text: Numbers game played with iPad, rules added

indicators.note: something played with is toyed with and moved around, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Countdown's numbers game is played on a tablet with extra rules.
explanation.walkthrough: Numbers means things that numb, not figures; the Numbers game is one round of the theme show Countdown.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinal anaesthetic injections, often given in childbirth, deaden sensation, so they are painkilling agents that numb.

clue.text: Support for stone channel

parts.note: st is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight of fourteen pounds
a rut is a groove or furrow worn in the ground

explanation.surface: A prop for a stone gutter carrying water.
explanation.walkthrough: The stone here is the weight unit, not a rock; the channel is a wheel groove, not a TV station.
explanation.definitionFit: A strut is a rod or bar in a framework that bears load and braces a structure.

clue.text: Stood out as a nail head in a brogue?

indicators.note: being in something means sitting within it, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a brogue is a type of leather shoe with decorative punched holes; the question mark flags this definition by example

indicators.note: the head of something is its top or front, so only the leading letter is kept

parts.note: first letter

explanation.surface: A hobnail's head sticking out of a brogue, standing proud of the leather.
explanation.walkthrough: A brogue is only one kind of footwear, hence the question mark; the surface suggests a nail poking through the sole.
explanation.definitionFit: To shine can mean to excel or be conspicuous, so it matches being prominent or excelling among others.

clue.text: Boatman's grown but yet to reach full potential

parts.note: Boatman is the setter, so the setter is = I am, contracted
grown up, fully developed

explanation.surface: The setter confesses he is grown up yet still not fully developed.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter naming himself means 'I'; with the apostrophe-s it becomes 'I am', and 'but' is a contrast joining the two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: Something still undeveloped or childish has not yet come into its adult or ripened state.

clue.text: Tree found where rock is extracted from mountain ashore

indicators.note: extracting something draws it out, so letters are taken away from the phrase

parts.note: ore is rock containing metal
with the rock removed from its end, the phrase names a tree, another name for the one wanted

explanation.surface: A tree grows on a mountain slope running down to the shore, where rock is quarried.
explanation.walkthrough: The deletion leaves 'mountain ash', which is not the answer but a second name for it, so the wordplay lands on a synonym rather than on letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The rowan, Sorbus aucuparia, with red berries, is also called the mountain ash, a common European tree.

clue.text: Bucks' consorts spoil poodles: lop pieces off

indicators.note: to spoil something is to mess it up, so the remaining letters are disordered
lopping cuts pieces away, so the named letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written
these three letters are removed

explanation.surface: The deer's mates indulge their poodles, then trim bits off them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lop' does double duty: it names the letters to cut and, with 'pieces off', says to cut them; the four left are then jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: A buck is a male deer, and its female partners are the hinds of fallow or roe deer.

clue.text: An equal to Earl Peel, the last of the shire

indicators.note: to peel is to strip something away, so the final letter is removed

parts.note: a shire is an English county

explanation.surface: Earl Peel sounds like a peer of the realm, ranked alongside another aristocrat from the shires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Earl Peel' reads as a title and a surname, but Peel is the instruction; 'the last of the shire' is what gets peeled away.
explanation.definitionFit: A European count holds the rank equivalent to a British earl in the nobility.

clue.text: Tools for measuring moulded replicas

indicators.note: moulding shapes material into a new form, so the letters take a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Measuring instruments made as cast copies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moulded replicas' sounds like casting copies, which fits a workshop; the word is simply rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Calipers are hinged instruments with two legs used to gauge thickness or diameter precisely.

clue.text: Blue feathers

definitions.meaning: first meaning: sad, low in spirits
second meaning: the fine soft plumage of birds, as in a duvet

explanation.walkthrough: Blue feathers suggests a colourful bird; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means low or depressed as an adjective and soft fluffy plumage as a noun.

clue.text: Boatman takes a second in meeting to get the information organised

indicators.note: being in something means sitting within it, so one group goes inside another

parts.note: a date is an appointment or meeting
AB is an able seaman, a sailor, standing for a boatman here
the article as written, taken on by the sailor
s is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: The setter takes a moment in a meeting to sort out the facts.
explanation.walkthrough: Boatman is the setter's pseudonym, but here it is read literally as a sailor, and AB (able seaman) is the usual crossword sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A database is a structured collection of data held so it can be searched, a store of facts arranged.

clue.text: Apology for metal found in food every year

indicators.note: what is found in something lies inside it, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: a meal is food eaten at one sitting
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
p.a. stands for per annum, Latin for each year

explanation.surface: Someone apologises because metal turned up in the food, year after year.
explanation.walkthrough: The metal slots in near the end of the food word, before its last letter, and the annual abbreviation follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase meaning 'through my fault' is an admission of guilt, used as a confession or regret.

clue.text: Trap large bird in flight; inert, remove skin

indicators.note: skinning strips off the outside, so the first and last letters go
flying means climbing upward, and in a down entry rising means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: the roc is the giant mythical bird of the Arabian Nights
the word without its outer letters

explanation.surface: Instructions for catching a huge bird as it flies, then skinning it once it is still.
explanation.walkthrough: The roc is the standard crossword giant bird; 'in flight' also looks like an anagram signal but here it means going up.
explanation.definitionFit: To corner someone is to force them into a position with no escape, so they are caught.

clue.text: Regularly amounting to a two-digit figure

parts.note: as in 'a sum of fifty', where the small word means amounting to
the smallest number written with two digits

explanation.surface: A total that keeps coming to a number in double figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' looks like an alternate-letter signal, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens frequently or many times occurs habitually, at short intervals.

clue.text: Wood consumed by one going up in flames

indicators.note: something consumed is swallowed up, so one piece disappears inside another

parts.note: taken as written
fir is a conifer and its timber

explanation.surface: Timber being devoured as a fire takes hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Consumed' plays on fire eating wood, which is exactly what the surface pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: Burning, ablaze: something alight is in the process of burning, the idiom for being in flames.

clue.text: Re-arrange ops for OAP

indicators.note: arranging puts things into a fresh order, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: all nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to reschedule operations for a pensioner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Re-arrange' looks like one anagram word, but the hyphen splits it: the first part is the definition. An OAP is an old-age pensioner.
explanation.definitionFit: Re, as in business letters, means concerning or with regard to, the same as this prepositional phrase.

clue.text: Fresh milk etc? Not initially

indicators.note: not at the start means the opening letter is left off

parts.note: dairy produce: milk, butter, cheese and so on

explanation.surface: Is milk and the like fresh? Not at first, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh' seems to describe the milk, but it is the definition, in its breezy sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An airy room is well ventilated and breezy, full of clean, cool, open air.

clue.text: Sustainable kind of approach to farming?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, split in two words: advice to grow crops rather than raise livestock

explanation.walkthrough: Split as BE ARABLE, the answer is a farming policy: arable farming grows crops on ploughed land. The question mark flags the whimsical split.
explanation.definitionFit: Sustainable in the sense of endurable or tolerable: something one can put up with or withstand.

clue.text: See 22
Accounts really starting to rise alarmingly — they need settling first!

indicators.note: the start of something is its beginning, so only the opening letters are kept

parts.note: first letters of the two words
a horse that rears rises up on its hind legs in alarm

explanation.surface: Debts are mounting worryingly, and they must be paid off before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: The accounting surface makes 'accounts' look like part of the definition, but it only lends a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Overdue debts or unpaid sums that have fallen behind must be cleared as a priority.

clue.text: Stand for letters game

indicators.note: being game means willing to play along, and what is at play gets shifted around

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An endorsement of Countdown's letters game, the round where contestants make words.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters game is a round of Countdown, this puzzle's theme, so 'game' looks like part of a name before being read as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A trestle is a framework of a beam on splayed legs used to support a tabletop.
